titleEn: Some states are stepping up after federal childcare cuts – and now offer lessons for the future
titleZh: 联邦托育经费削减后，一些州的应对能带来什么经验？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: While affordability pressures are hitting Americans in many facets of their lives, from groceries to gas prices to housing costs, one important expense often gets less attention – childcare.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然负担能力的压力在美国人生活的许多方面都受到了打击，从食品杂货到汽油价格再到住房成本，但一项重要的支出往往受到较少的关注-托儿。

paragraphs.en: After a huge infusion of federal funds into childcare dried up at the end of the Biden administration, experts warned that this sharp cutoff, sometimes dubbed the “childcare cliff,” would force parents to either scale back work to handle the extra caretaking or pay steep costs out of pocket.
paragraphs.zh: 在拜登政府结束时，大量联邦资金注入儿童保育后枯竭，专家警告说，这种急剧的切断，有时被称为“儿童保育悬崖”，将迫使父母要么缩减工作以处理额外的照顾，要么自掏腰包支付高昂的费用。

paragraphs.en: The potential effects of the federal cuts are hard to estimate, in part because states took different approaches in the aftermath. In some cases, they offset the sharp cuts in part by redirecting other funds to childcare.
paragraphs.zh: 联邦削减的潜在影响很难估计，部分原因是各州在之后采取了不同的做法。在某些情况下，他们通过将其他资金重新用于儿童保育来部分抵消大幅削减。

paragraphs.en: But several states, including Vermont, New Mexico and Kentucky, have gone further and innovated on their own to shore up support for working parents and their young children. Meanwhile, New York City is expanding free toddler slots for lower-income families, following Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s announcement to build a universal early childcare system.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，包括佛蒙特州、新墨西哥州和肯塔基州在内的几个州已经走得更远，自行创新，为在职父母及其年幼子女提供海岸。与此同时，在市长佐兰·马姆达尼（Zohran Mamdani）宣布建立一个普遍的幼儿保育系统之后，纽约市正在为低收入家庭扩大免费幼儿时段。

paragraphs.en: Taken together, these experiments point to bipartisan ways to support working parents, especially if the results of the November 2026 midterms signal a new willingness to tackle one of the biggest cost burdens for families.
paragraphs.zh: 总的来说，这些实验指出了支持在职父母的两党方法，特别是如果2026年11月中期选举的结果表明有新的意愿来解决家庭最大的成本负担之一。

paragraphs.en: As researchers of sociology and childcare policy with six children from 1 to 16 years old between us, we have also gained insights from our own data gathered over 75 interviews with parents in St. Louis, Missouri, over the past few years. We see them struggling with a fragmented childcare system that’s in need of a deep strategic investment. These families face limited choices and soaring costs for an essential good that allows a parent to go to work.
paragraphs.zh: 作为社会学和儿童保育政策的研究人员，我们之间有6个1到16岁的孩子，我们也从我们自己的数据中获得了见解，这些数据是在密苏里州圣路易斯对父母进行的75次采访中收集的，在过去的几年里。我们看到他们在支离破碎的儿童保育系统中苦苦挣扎，需要深入的战略投资。这些家庭面临着有限的选择和基本商品成本飙升的问题让父母可以去工作

paragraphs.en: Out-of-pocket expenses for parents using center-based care in childcare centers and private preschool programs have more than doubled since 2019. In 2024, the national average price of childcare was US$13,128 annually, which rivals housing as the most expensive item in family budgets.
paragraphs.zh: 自2019年以来，在托儿中心和私立学前教育项目中使用中心护理的父母的自付费用增加了一倍多。2024年，全国托儿服务的平均价格为每年13，128美元，与住房竞争，成为家庭预算中最昂贵的项目。

paragraphs.en: States go their own way
paragraphs.zh: 各州各行其是

paragraphs.en: The disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic laid bare the critical role that reliable, high-quality childcare plays for working families. But we believe it also presented an opportunity for innovative investments in the nation’s fractured childcare landscape.
paragraphs.zh: 2019冠状病毒病大流行造成的混乱暴露了可靠、高质量的托儿服务对工薪家庭的重要作用。但我们相信，这也为国家破碎的托儿服务格局提供了创新投资的机会。

paragraphs.en: Pandemic relief legislation in 2021 directed nearly $40 billion to shore up the supply and quality of childcare. This funding increase, which was a fourfold jump over previous levels, supported childcare staff with higher wages and allowed for other investments to improve the quality of care.
paragraphs.zh: 2021年的大流行病救济立法将近400亿美元用于海岸，以提高儿童保育的供应和质量。这一资金增长是以前水平的四倍，为儿童保育人员提供了更高的工资，并允许其他投资来提高护理质量。

paragraphs.en: The reach was vast, with stabilization funds flowing to 220,000 providers serving 9.6 million children. Many states also provided grants to create new slots and improve how providers got paid.
paragraphs.zh: 这一举措的覆盖面很广，稳定基金流向了22万个为960万儿童提供服务的机构。许多州还提供赠款，以创造新的名额，并改善提供服务的机构获得报酬的方式。

paragraphs.en: As those funds began drying up in September 2023, some states started to address these shortfalls on their own. In some cases, they took significant steps at a policy level to channel more support to working parents. We believe these investments could serve as examples for the rest of the country.
paragraphs.zh: 随着这些资金在2023年9月开始枯竭，一些州开始自行解决这些短缺问题。在某些情况下，他们在政策层面采取了重大措施，为在职父母提供更多支持。我们相信这些投资可以为美国其他地区提供榜样。

paragraphs.en: One is Vermont, which in 2023 became the first state to pass a law establishing a childcare entitlement. Following more than a decade of advocacy and bipartisan support, the law established a near-universal public childcare system, funded partially through a payroll tax of 0.44% split between employers and employees.
paragraphs.zh: 其中之一是佛蒙特州，该州于2023年成为第一个通过法律确立儿童保育权利的州。经过十多年的倡导和两党支持，该法律建立了一个近乎普遍的公共儿童保育系统，部分资金来自雇主和雇员分摊的0.44%的工资税。

paragraphs.en: Through an expansion of subsidies along income tiers, the number of families covered rose by 55% from July 2022 to May 2025, while flexible grants increased the number of providers and focused on improving the quality of care. About 12,000 children are now covered under this program.
paragraphs.zh: 通过沿着收入层次扩大补贴，从2022年7月到2025年5月，覆盖的家庭数量增加了55%，而灵活的赠款增加了提供者的数量，并专注于提高护理质量。该计划目前覆盖了约12，000名儿童。

paragraphs.en: New Mexico went even further. In November 2025, the state became the first in the nation to offer universal childcare. Based on an older program that provided free childcare to low-income families, the initiative expanded support to all working parents regardless of income.
paragraphs.zh: 新墨西哥州走得更远。2025年11月，该州成为全国第一个提供全民托儿服务的州。该计划以向低收入家庭提供免费托儿服务的旧计划为基础，将支持范围扩大到所有在职父母，无论收入如何。

paragraphs.en: Before the expansion, 32,000 children were covered, a number the state aims to double by 2028. On average, the state estimates that the program will save families $12,000 a year.
paragraphs.zh: 在扩大之前，有32,000名儿童被覆盖，该州的目标是到2028年翻一番。该州估计，该计划平均每年将为家庭节省12,000美元。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the Kentucky legislature in April 2026 passed a measure with strong bipartisan support to make major investments in the state’s childcare infrastructure. Key provisions include free childcare for the children of childcare center employees, increased state-subsidized reimbursement rates, and required training to support very young special needs children.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，肯塔基州立法机构在2026年4月通过了一项得到两党大力支持的措施，对该州的托儿基础设施进行重大投资。关键条款包括为托儿中心员工的子女提供免费托儿服务，提高国家补贴的报销率，以及为支持年幼的特殊需要儿童提供必要的培训。

paragraphs.en: The Kentucky measure also loosened regulations that had made it tough for employers to share costs for care, such as renting facilities, while pitching a pilot program to open one-room “microcenters” in communities that lacked sufficient childcare options. In addition, Gov. Andy Beshear launched a complementary Pre-K for All pilot program in several counties.
paragraphs.zh: 肯塔基州的这项措施还放宽了一些规定，这些规定使雇主很坚韧分担托儿费用，比如租用设施，同时还推出了一个试点项目，在缺乏足够托儿选择的社区开设一个房间的“微型中心”。此外，州长安迪·贝希尔（Andy Beshear）在几个县推出了一个补充性的“全民学前教育”试点项目。

paragraphs.en: Another example is New York City, where Mamdani has announced an expansion for toddlers as young as 2 years old in all five of the city’s boroughs, building on the city’s programs for free childcare for 3-K and pre-K. To date, this effort has increased some slots, although the rollout in September hit bumps.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个例子是纽约市，Mamdani已经宣布在该市所有五个行政区扩大2岁的幼儿，建立在该市的3-K和学前儿童免费托儿计划的基础上。

paragraphs.en: The childcare crunch by the numbers
paragraphs.zh: 儿童保育危机的数字

paragraphs.en: Given the skyrocketing costs, over 70% of families who sought care say it’s difficult to find childcare – and that doesn’t count the 11% who fail to find any at all, according to a 2023 government survey. That report found that families with Black or Hispanic children or infants, and those living in the South and West, are more likely to run into cost as a barrier.
paragraphs.zh: 根据2023年的一项政府调查，考虑到飞涨的成本，超过70%的寻求护理的家庭表示很难找到托儿服务-这还不包括11%的根本找不到托儿服务的家庭。该报告发现，有黑人或西班牙裔儿童或婴儿的家庭，以及那些生活在南部和西部的家庭，更有可能遇到成本这一障碍。

paragraphs.en: On the supply side, three-quarters of providers say they have to turn many families away or put them on waiting lists. Center-based care for an infant costs more than in-state college tuition at a public university in 32 states, yet childcare workers, who are overwhelmingly women of color, earn the same as parking lot attendants and dog walkers. That makes them some of the lowest-paid workers in the entire economy.
paragraphs.zh: 在供给方面，四分之三的服务提供者表示，他们不得不拒绝许多家庭，或者把他们列入等待名单。在32个州，以中心为基础的婴儿护理费用比公立大学的学费还要高，然而，儿童保育员--绝大多数是有色人种女性--的收入与停车场服务员和遛狗员一样。这使他们成为整个经济中收入最低的工人之一。

paragraphs.en: Amid soaring costs and scarce supply, roughly half of all U.S. families live in so-called childcare deserts – areas where there are three children under 5 for every licensed-care slot. The answer for many families in these cases is to rely on ad hoc and irregular informal care. Some parents told us they’re turning to relatives and neighbors for help. Others resorted to using unlicensed, and potentially unsafe, childcare providers because they found no other viable options. And for some remote workers, the daunting solution is to care for their kids themselves while working.
paragraphs.zh: 在成本飙升和供应稀缺的情况下，大约一半的美国家庭生活在所谓的儿童保育沙漠中--在这些地区，每个有执照的保育名额都有三个5岁以下的孩子。在这种情况下，许多家庭的解决办法是依靠临时和不定期的非正式护理。一些父母告诉我们，他们正在向亲戚和邻居寻求帮助。其他人则求助于使用无执照的，可能不安全的，因为他们找不到其他可行的选择。对于一些远程工作者来说，令人生畏的解决方案是在工作时自己照顾孩子。

paragraphs.en: The problem with such makeshift arrangements is that they tend, on average, to offer fewer of the learning opportunities linked to children’s long-term development and social mobility. And even these arrangements can be tough to afford: One single mother we interviewed told us she paid for a week’s childcare in kind with her own breast milk, which went to feed the care provider’s grandchildren. We also spoke to parents who reported choosing between childcare bills and heat, electricity or rent.
paragraphs.zh: 这种临时安排的问题在于，平均而言，它们提供的与儿童长期发展和社会流动性有关的学习机会较少。我们采访的一位单身母亲告诉我们，她用自己的母乳支付了一周的托儿费，我们还采访了一些父母，他们报告说，他们在育儿账单和暖气、电费或房租之间做出了选择。

paragraphs.en: Another mom told us about a more unconventional solution. She and her husband work full time but can’t afford the childcare options in their community, so she decided to join a gym that provides free childcare while its members exercise. She brings her laptop and works, rather than working out, while her toddler plays.
paragraphs.zh: 另一位母亲告诉我们一个更非传统的解决方案。她和丈夫都有全职工作，但负担不起社区的托儿服务，所以她决定加入一家健身房，在会员锻炼时提供免费托儿服务。她带着笔记本电脑工作，而不是在孩子玩耍时锻炼。

paragraphs.en: These parents are scraping by in the absence of the affordable, subsidized childcare options commonplace in other countries. But this crunch is also a lose-lose proposition for the economy. The U.S. could lose as much as $290 billion per year by 2030 in forgone economic activity due to women not working or not working as much due to childcare pressures, according to the consultancy BCG.
paragraphs.zh: 由于缺乏其他国家常见的负担得起的、有补贴的托儿服务，这些父母只能勉强度日。但这场危机对经济来说也是一个双输的命题。咨询公司BCG的数据显示，到2030年，由于女性不工作或由于育儿压力而不工作，美国每年可能因放弃经济活动而损失高达2900亿美元。

paragraphs.en: A path forward
paragraphs.zh: 一条前进的道路

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration has laid out its own vision. Vice President JD Vance announced in September 2026 a preliminary proposal to repurpose existing funds for childcare subsidies as a cash transfer to married parents, provided that one spouse stays home. We believe, however, this approach fails to reflect the real needs of the millions of U.S. parents who can’t pay their bills if they only get one paycheck. In fact, under the subsidy program that Vance cited, only 16% of eligible children are reached today anyway.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府已经制定了自己的愿景。副总统JD万斯在2026年9月宣布了一项初步提案，将现有的儿童保育补贴资金重新用于向已婚父母提供现金转移，前提是配偶一方留在家中。然而，我们认为，这种做法未能反映数百万美国父母的真实的需求，他们如果只拿到一份薪水就无法支付账单。事实上，根据万斯引用的补贴计划，今天只有16%的符合条件的儿童得到了帮助。

paragraphs.en: We believe, based on our research, that any comprehensive overhaul has four important components.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认为，根据我们的研究，任何全面改革都有四个重要组成部分。

paragraphs.en: First is a robust national policy for paid family leave, which would let families make the best care decisions for newborns, infants and parents themselves rather than sprinting back to work. Paid family leave would also ease demand for scarce infant care in the market.
paragraphs.zh: 首先是一项强有力的带薪家庭假国家政策，这将使家庭能够为新生儿、婴儿和父母自己做出最好的护理决定，而不是赶回工作岗位。带薪家庭假还将缓解市场上对稀缺的婴儿护理的需求。

paragraphs.en: Second is an expansion of early childhood care and education programs. By publicly subsidizing childcare, particularly for low-income families and special needs kids, policymakers can help close the affordability gap for high-quality care.
paragraphs.zh: 其次是扩大幼儿保育和教育项目。通过公共补贴儿童保育，特别是低收入家庭和有特殊需要的儿童，政策制定者可以帮助缩小高质量保育的负担能力差距。

paragraphs.en: Third is a greater investment in childcare workers. Qualified caregivers are the cornerstone of high-quality childcare. If their wages and working conditions improve, it means fewer will have to take side hustles or quit for better jobs.
paragraphs.zh: 第三，加大对儿童保育员的投资。合格的保育员是高质量儿童保育的基石。如果他们的工资和工作条件得到改善，这意味着将有更少的人不得不兼职或辞职去找更好的工作。

paragraphs.en: Finally, providers will need more incentives to open in underserved areas. Childcare is expensive to provide and runs on thin margins. In low-income and rural areas, many families can’t pay prices that cover the true cost of care, and subsidy payments are often set below that cost. So opening a center there doesn’t make much financial sense. Startup grants, higher subsidy rates and operating support help close that gap, which makes it possible to open and stay open where need is greatest.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，提供者需要更多的激励措施，才能在服务水平低下的地区开设幼儿园。提供托儿服务的成本很高，而且利润微薄。在低收入和农村地区，许多家庭支付的价格无法覆盖真正的托儿成本，而补贴金额往往低于成本。因此，在那里开设一个中心在财务上没有多大意义。启动赠款、更高的补贴率和运营支持有助于缩小这一差距，这使得在最需要的地方开放并保持开放成为可能。
